extra_snippets: Axos Financial is acquiring Arc Technologies, the AI-native cash management platform, in a deal closing July 2026. With large banks approving only 13–15% of small business loans and fintech lenders now originating 32% of them, the acquisition shows why clean, real-time books are becoming your credit application.

On the surface this looks like a routine fintech M&A story — a bank acquires a startup, press release goes out, deal closes, everyone moves on. But the specifics of who's buying whom, and why, say something bigger about where small business banking is headed, and what business owners should expect (and demand) from their financial institutions over the next few years. Axos Financial announced in early July 2026 that its subsidiary, Axos Nevada Holding, has agreed to acquire Arc Technologies.

Axos, for its part, is explicit about why it wants this: the deal is meant to strengthen its ability to serve what the company calls "structurally underserved small businesses" and to fold Arc's AI-driven financial infrastructure into Axos's broader digital banking stack. The transaction is expected to close by the end of July 2026 and, notably, isn't expected to move the needle much on Axos's overall financial results — this is a capability acquisition, not a revenue play.
